mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months compared to non-tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from baseline when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during periods of sustained high unemployment (>5.5% for two months) compared to periods below that threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation between four-month INDPRO declines and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with deflationary pressure, which historically precedes equity market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% MoM
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with deflation fears
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.5% MoM compared to other periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above trend by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > trend +10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of sustained above-trend housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of rapid payroll employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes equity market corrections as consumers delay purchases, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation between coordinated increases in RSAFS and decreases in GDPC1 over two quarters and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.
